summary: High-rate 429s for interactive chat after enabling SDK session_replay telemetry
description:
Issue summary:
Nimbus Analytics reports intermittent 429 throttles for low-latency chat sessions that started immediately after they enabled the SDK 'session_replay' telemetry feature (client-side keystroke/interaction capture). Throttles coincide with periods of apparently low interactive traffic (user idle windows) and occur across multiple user sessions.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency and 429s on interactive chat endpoints for a subset (~3-5%) of active sessions during nightly hours and occasional daytime spikes.
- Affects multiple product users and prevents real-time typing UX for affected sessions.

Environment:
- Customer: Nimbus Analytics (enterprise) on Redwood Private (VPC) using a dedicated pool in eu-west.
- SDK: rust-sdk v1.6.2 with session_replay enabled and telemetry_endpoint configured to use same API key as production calls.
- Models in path: gpt-redwood-24k (primary), fallback to gpt-open-3b.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a chat session in the Nimbus web app with session_replay enabled.
2) Leave the session idle for 60-90s (SDK configured to flush buffered keystroke events every 30s).
3) Re-enter and start typing; observe occasional 429 on the next generation call.
4) Repeat with multiple browser tabs/orchestrated workers to increase concurrency.

Observed behavior:
- Telemetry flushes appear as short bursts of small requests (0-50 tokens each) originating from the SDK on the same API key used for generation.
- The bursts align with the token/token-window accounting in our rate-limiter and are depleting the per-tenant token/concurrency window leading to 429 responses on user-facing calls.
- Console shows tenant-level token-window exhaustion at the same timestamps as customer errors.

Expected behavior:
- Telemetry/diagnostic pings should not consume production token/concurrency quota or should be accounted separately to avoid impacting user-facing generation.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- SDK config snippet (session_replay: true, flush_interval_ms: 30000).
- Timestamps and sample request IDs for failed generations: req-6fc2a9, req-6fc2b1, req-6fc2e7.
- Sample telemetry flush logs showing hundreds of tiny POSTs during a 10-minute window.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:42 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Opened case after Nimbus escalated via account manager. Collected initial SDK config and sample request ids. Customer reports issue started immediately after toggling session_replay in v1.6.2.

2026-03-10 12:05 UTC - Sofia Chen (SRE): Confirmed tenant token-window exhaustion in eu-west around the reported timestamps. Correlated spikes with small telemetry POSTs from the customer's edge IP range. Rate-limiter logs show multiple short token drains from ephemeral short requests counted against the same tenant quota.

2026-03-10 15:20 UTC - Tom Blake (Nimbus engineer): Provided orchestration details — they fan out SDK instances for multi-tab journeys and rely on SDK-level flush to reduce network chatter. By design telemetry uses same API key; assumed it wouldn’t be quota counted.
investigation_notes: Confirmed telemetry endpoint calls are routed through api-gateway and pass through the same token accounting path as generation requests.

Rate-limiter uses per-tenant token windows that count all requests authenticated with the tenant's API keys; small telemetry requests still increment token accounting due to header metadata mapping to the same route.
Observed periodic flush pattern every ~30s from SDK; when many sessions/tabs are open, aggregated bursts coincide with window exhaustion in the short refill interval configuration.
No evidence of hardware or dedicated pool capacity shortage; this is purely quota accounting at the gateway/rate-limiter layer.
Edge-case: private VPC sidecars add a small amplification due to connection pooling and retries; increases apparent concurrency briefly during flush times.
Temporary mitigation test: instructing customer to set SDK flush_interval_ms to 300000 (5 min) reduced burst frequency and eliminated 429s in a small A/B test.
resolution:
Workaround provided and roadmap fix identified. Actions taken:
1) Workaround (customer applied): Change SDK session_replay config to use an isolated telemetry API key or increase flush interval to avoid synchronized bursts. After the change, Nimbus saw immediate reduction in 429s during nightly windows.
2) Short-term platform mitigation: SRE added an exclusion rule for the customer's telemetry route in the rate-limiter config to stop counting telemetry pings against the tenant token window while we test. This is scoped to the customer's dedicated VPC and will be rolled back after full fix validation.
3) Long-term fix: Engineering to add route-level token-accounting flags so telemetry/endpoints can be marked non-consumptive or redirected to a separate quota pool. Patch PR created and under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5821.

Follow-ups:
- Eng to add clearer SDK docs recommending use of separate telemetry keys for production traffic and provide sample config for flush intervals and batching.
- Product to evaluate telemetry as a first-class traffic class with separate quota allocation on Private/Dedicated deployments.
- SRE to monitor the customer's tenant quota telemetry for 72 hours post-mitigation.

Status: In Progress — workaround validated by customer; engineering PR in review; monitoring active.
